related.title: TAU：跨rank因果順序與時鐘修正界線
related.titleEn: TAU: cross-rank causality and clock-correction bounds
related.why: 用兩課的可觀察驗收條件比較模型邊界：接手者能重現28與60並說明量綱；不因數值變大就推論機器整體吞吐量提高。
related.whyEn: Compare model boundaries using observable acceptance criteria: The receiver reproduces both values with correct units and does not infer improved whole-machine throughput merely from a larger active-rank average.
related.difference: 使用原創合成資料研究「TAU：跨rank因果順序與時鐘修正界線」，從物理或資料契約推導計算，並以反例驗證。完成：交付原始與修正時間、message配對、約束表及不可行反例；原始trace不覆寫，並明示未估計時鐘不確定性與網路延遲。
related.differenceEn: Investigate TAU: cross-rank causality and clock-correction bounds using an original synthetic fixture. Derive the calculation from its physical or data contract, challenge it with a counterexample, and defend a bounded conclusion. Complete: Deliver raw and corrected timestamps, message matches, constraint tables and an infeasible counterexample. Preserve original traces and explicitly state that clock uncertainty and physical network latency have not been estimated.
related.transfer: 保留單位與邊界條件，僅轉移可證明相容的驗證方法。
related.transferEn: Retain units and boundary conditions; transfer only demonstrably compatible verification methods.
practice: 先計每列100與20，再算未加權平均60；另外從work與active_seconds加總得28，將差異連回1秒與9秒的權重。
將兩個前向條件寫成95+delta≥101與102+delta≥111，分別得到6與9；使用最大下界，而非平均兩個offset需求。
比較兩個模型的輸入、誤差與驗收條件，記錄不能沿用的假設。
practiceEn: Calculate row rates of one hundred and twenty and their unweighted mean of sixty. Separately sum work and active time to obtain twenty-eight, and trace the disagreement to one second versus nine seconds of exposure rather than treating one expression as universally correct.

Write the forward constraints as 95 plus delta at least 101 and 102 plus delta at least 111. Derive bounds six and nine and explain why their maximum, rather than their average, satisfies both inequalities simultaneously.
Compare inputs, errors, and criteria; document assumptions that cannot be transferred.

related.title: Polaris：共享 PCIe 上游切面的超額需求
related.titleEn: Polaris: oversubscription at a shared PCIe upstream cut
related.why: 用兩課的可觀察驗收條件比較模型邊界：接手者能重現28與60並說明量綱；不因數值變大就推論機器整體吞吐量提高。
related.whyEn: Compare model boundaries using observable acceptance criteria: The receiver reproduces both values with correct units and does not infer improved whole-machine throughput merely from a larger active-rank average.
related.difference: 畫有向路徑圖，以 edge_id 展開每條流；在共同邊累加需求並保留端點與切面兩種報表。
related.differenceEn: Represent the topology as directed edges and expand each flow into edge identifiers. Aggregate demand on shared edges while preserving separate endpoint and cut reports, so an endpoint maximum cannot hide an upstream bottleneck.
related.transfer: 保留單位與邊界條件，僅轉移可證明相容的驗證方法。
related.transferEn: Retain units and boundary conditions; transfer only demonstrably compatible verification methods.
practice: 先計每列100與20，再算未加權平均60；另外從work與active_seconds加總得28，將差異連回1秒與9秒的權重。

教學切面的超額需求為 max(0,兩流需求總和－切面容量)。只分析流量守恆與排隊傾向，不推定實際 GPU 直傳路徑；共享切面容量 16 GB/s；兩流各需求 12，變更為各 8 GB/s，其他路徑不設瓶頸；名義式 max(0,12+12-16) = 8 GB/s；變更式 max(0,8+8-16) = 0 GB/s。所有數值、限制與門檻為原創合成教學條件；來源支援概念與介面，不代表實機量測或設備規格。
比較兩個模型的輸入、誤差與驗收條件，記錄不能沿用的假設。
practiceEn: Calculate row rates of one hundred and twenty and their unweighted mean of sixty. Separately sum work and active time to obtain twenty-eight, and trace the disagreement to one second versus nine seconds of exposure rather than treating one expression as universally correct.

Model excess offered load as the positive difference between aggregate demand and cut capacity. This is a conservation constraint, not proof of the actual peer-transfer path, protocol efficiency or achieved throughput. Use a synthetic 16 GB/s cut shared by two flows. Each initially demands 12 GB/s, then 8 GB/s. Other links are assumed nonlimiting, and rates use decimal GB consistently. Nominal max(0,12+12-16) = 8 GB/s; changed max(0,8+8-16) = 0 GB/s. Every numeric input, limit and threshold is an original synthetic teaching condition. References establish concepts and interfaces, not measured machine results or equipment specifications.
Compare inputs, errors, and criteria; document assumptions that cannot be transferred.
